lesson_basicsIsolatedHonour_explain: The Red Dragon connects to nothing else in your hand. Discarding it keeps every set and partial set, and leaves you one tile from winning.
lesson_basicsTwoSidedWait_prompt: Your hand is one tile from complete. Select every tile that wins.
lesson_basicsTwoSidedWait_explain: 4-5 Characters is open at both ends: a 3 or a 6 completes the run. That is twice the chances of a wait that is open at one end only.
lesson_basicsKeepTwoSided_prompt: Which discard leaves you waiting on the most tiles?
lesson_basicsKeepTwoSided_explain: Discarding the 5 Characters keeps 2-3, which waits on a 1 or a 4. Keeping 3-5 instead waits on the 4 alone.
lesson_basicsPairWait_title: Two pairs, two ways to win
lesson_basicsPairWait_prompt: Your hand is one tile from complete. Select every tile that wins.
lesson_basicsPairWait_explain: With two pairs, either one can become a pung while the other stays as the pair: an East Wind or a White Dragon wins.
lesson_basicsSimpleHand_prompt: You drew your winning tile. How many faan is the hand worth?
lesson_basicsSimpleHand_explain: All sequences (1), self-drawn (1) and fully concealed (1) make 3 faan, exactly the minimum to win. Your flower belongs to another seat, so it scores nothing, and holding it means no faan for having no flowers.
lesson_basicsDiscardWin_prompt: You can win on this discard. How many faan is the hand worth?
lesson_basicsDiscardWin_explain: Characters with honours is a half flush (3), and the Green Dragon pung adds 1: 4 faan. A discard win scores nothing for self-drawn, and your exposed pung rules out fully concealed.
lesson_basicsAllCopiesVisible_prompt: East is close to winning. Which tile can you discard with certainty that it is safe?
lesson_basicsAllCopiesVisible_explain: Three West Winds are in the discards and you hold the fourth. Nobody else can hold one, so nobody can be waiting on it. The lonely 6 Bamboo is exactly what East is waiting for.
lesson_basicsNoChance_prompt: East is close to winning. Which tile can no run be waiting on?
lesson_basicsNoChance_explain: All four 2 Characters are visible. A run with the 1 Characters must be 1-2-3, so no run can be waiting on it. Only a pair or pung wait could still take it, which is rare.
lesson_basicsTutorial_welcome: Welcome to the table. You sit at the bottom as East, the dealer. Play goes counter-clockwise: you, then South on your right, West opposite and North on your left.
lesson_basicsTutorial_yourHand: These are your 13 tiles. A winning hand is four sets and a pair. A set is three in a row of one suit (a chow) or three of a kind (a pung).
lesson_basicsTutorial_draw: North discarded, so it is your turn: you drew a tile from the wall. You now hold 14, so discard one.
lesson_basicsTutorial_discardFirst: Discard the Green Dragon. It is on its own and nothing can join it into a set.
lesson_basicsTutorial_pungOffer: South discarded an East Wind and you hold two. You can claim any player's discard to complete a pung (碰).
lesson_basicsTutorial_pungLaid: Your East pung is laid face up. East is both your seat wind and the round wind, so it is worth 2 faan. After a claim you discard without drawing.
lesson_basicsTutorial_chowOffer: North, on your left, discarded the 4 Characters, which makes a run with your 3 and 5. You can chow (上) only the discard of the player on your left.
lesson_basicsTutorial_kongOffer: South discarded the 9 Dots and you hold three. Four of a kind is a kong (槓).
lesson_basicsTutorial_replacement: A kong uses four tiles but counts as one set, so you drew a replacement tile from the end of the wall.
lesson_basicsTutorial_discardAfterKong: Discard the White Dragon. Now you need only a second 2 Dots.
lesson_basicsTutorial_selfDrawn: You drew the 2 Dots yourself, and your hand is complete. Winning on your own draw is self-drawn (自摸), and all three players pay.
lesson_basicsTutorial_result: The hand scores 4 faan: the East pung 2, self-drawn 1 and no flowers 1. That clears the 3 faan minimum, and each player pays you.
lesson_minedWaits_prompt: Your hand is one tile from complete. Select every tile that wins with at least the minimum faan.
lesson_minedEfficiency_prompt: Which discard keeps your hand closest to winning, with the most tiles left to improve it?
lesson_minedEfficiency_explain: Discard {tiles}: {count} unseen tiles then move your hand forward.
lesson_minedDefenceAllCopiesVisible_prom: An opponent is close to winning. Which tile can you tell is safe from what you can see?
lesson_minedDefenceAllCopiesVisible_expl: {tiles}: every copy is visible, so nobody can be waiting on it.
lesson_minedDefenceNoChance_prompt: An opponent is close to winning. Which tile can you tell is safe from what you can see?
lesson_minedDefenceNoChance_explain: {tiles}: every run through it needs a tile whose four copies are all visible, so no run can be waiting on it.
lesson_minedDefenceGenbutsu_prompt: An opponent is close to winning. Which tile can you tell is safe from what you can see?
lesson_minedDefenceGenbutsu_explain: {tiles}: every opponent has already discarded it. Hong Kong rules let a player win on a tile they discarded earlier, so this is a hint rather than a guarantee, but here it holds.
lesson_minedFaanSelfDraw_prompt: You drew your winning tile. How many faan is the hand worth?
lesson_minedFaanDiscard_prompt: You can win on this discard. How many faan is the hand worth?
